title: Tropical Storm Lala Soaks Hawaii with Huge Rain!
summary:
Hawaii is getting soaked! Tropical Storm Lala, which used to be a hurricane, is moving across the islands and bringing super heavy rain and strong winds. On Sunday, more than 130,000 homes and businesses had no electricity. That's a lot of people sitting in the dark!

The storm is especially hard on the Big Island. Some mountain areas might get up to 35 inches of rain—that's almost three feet! Imagine water up to your waist. All that rain is making rivers overflow and could cause mudslides. The wind is also super strong, blowing palm trees around and making the ocean waves crash hard.

Sadly, one person died in a car accident during the storm. Also, 19 roofs were blown off houses! The governor, Josh Green, said rescue teams are searching for people after flash floods swept some homes off their foundations in two coastal towns. That sounds really scary.

People are trying to stay safe. Shelters are open, and many folks are staying inside. One man named Bobby Camara, who is 75, said he's just going to "hunker down, cross my fingers, hope the lights don't go out." Another resident, Mike Caputo, has a big water tank and a generator ready. He's worried about falling trees, especially a kind called albizia that grows really big but isn't very strong.

The storm is moving west, so Maui, Oahu, and Kauai are getting hit next. Forecasters say Lala might get stronger again after it passes Hawaii. For now, everyone is hoping the rain stops soon and the power comes back on.
why_it_matters: This shows why being ready for big storms—with flashlights, water, and a safe place to stay—can keep you and your family safer when the power goes out.

background_read: Hawaii is a group of islands in the Pacific Ocean where warm ocean water can make tropical storms stronger.
Governor Josh Green (Hawaii's state leader) helps organize emergency shelters and rescue teams during disasters.
The albizia tree is a fast-growing but weak tree that often causes damage when winds blow through Hawaii.
Article_Structure: WHO: Hawaii residents, Governor Josh Green, and rescue teams working after the storm.
WHAT: Tropical Storm Lala soaked the islands, knocked out power to more than 130,000 homes and businesses, and damaged houses.
WHERE: The Big Island was hit hardest, with Maui, Oahu, and Kauai next in the storm's path.
WHY: The storm, which had been a hurricane, brought extreme rain and winds that caused flash floods, mudslides, and dangerous conditions.
